learn: In Spanish, we say hola (OH-lah) to say hello. The h is quiet, so it sounds like "oh-la".
We say adiós (ah-dee-OHS) to say goodbye.
Wave your hand when you say hola and when you say adiós.
check: How do you say hello in Spanish?
How do you say goodbye in Spanish?
In hola, the letter h is...
lessons.try: Wave to three people at home and say hola. Later, wave and say adiós.

learn: In the morning we say buenos días. It means good morning.
In the afternoon we say buenas tardes. At night we say buenas noches.
Buenas noches also means good night when you go to bed.
check: What do you say in the morning?
What do you say at bedtime?
lessons.try: Say buenos días at breakfast and buenas noches at bedtime today.

learn: Por favor means please. Gracias means thank you.
When someone says gracias, you can answer de nada. It means you are welcome.
Kind words help everyone feel happy at school.
check: How do you say thank you?
What do you say after someone says gracias?
lessons.try: Use por favor and gracias at dinner tonight.

learn: ¿Qué tal? means "How's it going?"
You can answer bien (fine) or muy bien (very well).
Friends say it to each other every day.
lessons.try: Ask three friends "¿Qué tal?" and listen to their answers.

learn: Hasta luego means "see you later".
Hasta mañana means "see you tomorrow".
Use them when you leave.
check: We say hasta luego when we...
lessons.try: Say hasta mañana to your teacher at home time.

learn: Señor is Mr. or sir.
Señora is Mrs. or ma'am.
Señorita is Miss.
lessons.try: Greet your teacher with "Buenos días, señor" or "señora".

learn: Buenos días, clase means good morning, class.
The class answers: Buenos días, maestra (or maestro).
Maestra is a woman teacher; maestro is a man teacher.
lessons.try: Practise the morning greeting with the class.

learn: Sing: "Hola, hola, ¿cómo estás?"
Clap on each hola.
Songs help us remember words.
lessons.try: Sing the hello song with motions.

learn: Hola, adiós, hasta luego.
Buenos días, buenas noches.
Por favor, gracias.
lessons.try: Act out meeting and leaving a friend.

learn: To tell someone your name, say me llamo and then your name. Me llamo Ana means my name is Ana.
Point to yourself when you say me llamo.
Say it slowly: meh YAH-moh.
check: What do you say before your name?
When you say me llamo, you point to...
lessons.try: Tell three toys or people your name in Spanish: me llamo...

learn: To ask someone's name, say ¿cómo te llamas? It means what is your name?
Spanish questions start with an upside-down question mark ¿ and end with ?.
Your friend answers: me llamo and their name.
check: How do you ask someone's name?
The answer to ¿cómo te llamas? starts with...
lessons.try: Ask a grown-up ¿cómo te llamas? and listen to the answer.

learn: When you meet someone new, say mucho gusto. It means nice to meet you.
You can shake hands or wave when you say it.
Now you can have a little talk: hola, me llamo..., ¿cómo te llamas?, mucho gusto!
check: When do you say mucho gusto?
Which comes first when you meet someone?
lessons.try: Act out meeting a new friend with a stuffed animal, using all four phrases.

learn: Spanish letters have their own names: a, be, ce.
Spell your name with a partner.
Some letters sound different.
check: In Spanish, the letter b is called...
The letter a in Spanish sounds like...
lessons.try: Spell your name using Spanish letter names.

learn: ¿Y tú? means "And you?"
"Me llamo Ana. ¿Y tú?"
It passes the question back.
check: After "Me llamo Ana. ¿Y tú?" you say...
lessons.try: Pass "¿Y tú?" around the circle.

learn: ¿Cuántos años tienes? means "How old are you?"
Answer: Tengo cinco años (I am five).
Show your age on your fingers.
check: Tengo cinco años means I am...
Tengo seis años means I am...
lessons.try: Ask and answer your age.

learn: Niño means boy.
Niña means girl.
Niños can mean children.
lessons.try: Sort pictures into niño and niña.

learn: Amigo is a friend who is a boy; amiga is a friend who is a girl.
Mi amigo means my friend.
Introduce a friend: Este es mi amigo.
check: Este es mi amigo introduces a...
lessons.try: Introduce a friend to the class.

learn: Me llamo.
¿Cómo te llamas?
Mucho gusto.
lessons.try: Make a name badge and introduce yourself.

learn: Rojo means red. Azul means blue. Amarillo means yellow.
An apple can be rojo. The sky is azul. The sun is amarillo.
These three colors mix to make many others.
lessons.try: Find something rojo, something azul and something amarillo in your house.

learn: Verde means green. Naranja means orange. Morado means purple.
Grass is verde. An orange is naranja, just like its color. Grapes can be morado.
Blue and yellow make verde. Red and yellow make naranja.
lessons.try: Draw grass in verde, an orange in naranja and grapes in morado.

learn: Blanco means white. Negro means black. Rosa means pink. Café means brown.
Snow is blanco. The night sky is negro. A flamingo is rosa. Chocolate is café.
Ask ¿de qué color es? to mean what color is it?
lessons.try: Play a game: point to something and ask ¿de qué color es? A grown-up answers in Spanish.

learn: Find things around the room by colour.
Say the colour in Spanish.
"¡Rojo!" for a red book.
lessons.try: Play "Veo, veo" (I spy) with colours.

learn: El sol es amarillo (the sun is yellow).
La hoja es verde (the leaf is green).
La nieve es blanca (snow is white).
lessons.try: Draw three nature things and label the colours.

learn: Rojo + amarillo = naranja.
Azul + amarillo = verde.
Rojo + azul = morado.
lessons.try: Mix paints and name the new colours.

learn: Arcoíris means rainbow.
Name the colours of the rainbow.
Rojo, naranja, amarillo, verde, azul, morado.
check: The first colour of the rainbow is...
The last colour we say is...
lessons.try: Paint a rainbow and say each colour.

learn: Mi color favorito es azul.
Ask: ¿Cuál es tu color favorito?
Make a class graph.
check: Mi color favorito es... means My favourite ___ is...
¿Cuál es tu color favorito? asks your favourite...
Favourite colours can be shown in a...
lessons.try: Ask five friends their favourite colour.

learn: Eleven colour words.
Mixing.
Favourites.
lessons.try: Colour a picture following Spanish directions.

learn: Count with me: uno (1), dos (2), tres (3), cuatro (4), cinco (5).
Hold up one finger for each number.
Cinco is a whole hand of fingers.
lessons.try: Count five steps in Spanish as you walk.

learn: Keep counting: seis (6), siete (7), ocho (8), nueve (9), diez (10).
Diez is all the fingers on both hands.
Say them in order from uno to diez.
lessons.try: Count ten jumps in Spanish.

learn: To ask how many, say ¿cuántos? (KWAN-tohs).
If there are four apples, you answer cuatro.
Counting in Spanish works just like counting in English, one at a time.
lessons.try: Line up some toys. Ask ¿cuántos? and count them in Spanish.

learn: Uno, dos, tres on your fingers.
Show the right number.
Count to diez.
lessons.try: Count fingers in Spanish with a partner.

learn: Hop on each square and say the number.
Uno to diez.
Say it loud.
lessons.try: Play number hopscotch.

learn: Diez, nueve, ocho...
Like a rocket blast-off.
¡Despegue! means blast-off.
lessons.try: Count down from diez and jump.

learn: Uno más uno son dos.
Más means plus.
Son means equals.
lessons.try: Solve three finger sums in Spanish.

learn: Cero means zero.
Cero is nothing.
Count from cero to diez.
lessons.try: Show cero with an empty hand.

learn: Cero to diez.
Forward and back.
Adding.
lessons.try: Number bingo.

learn: Mamá means mom. Papá means dad.
La familia means the family.
Families can be big or small, and every family is special.
lessons.try: Draw your family and say la familia when you show it.

learn: Hermano means brother. Hermana means sister.
A bebé is a baby.
Words that end in o are often for boys, and words that end in a are often for girls.
lessons.try: Tell someone about a brother, sister or cousin using hermano or hermana.

learn: Abuelo means grandpa. Abuela means grandma.
Many families call grandma abuelita, which means dear little grandma.
Say te quiero to a person you love. It means I love you.
lessons.try: Call or hug someone you love and say te quiero.

learn: Bebé means baby.
Mi hermanito means my little brother; mi hermanita means my little sister.
Babies are small: pequeño.
lessons.try: Draw a baby and say bebé.

learn: Tía is aunt, tío is uncle.
Primo or prima is cousin.
Families can be big.
lessons.try: Count your tíos and primos.

learn: Casa means house.
Mi familia vive en una casa.
Rooms: la cocina (kitchen), el cuarto (bedroom).
lessons.try: Draw your casa and label two rooms.

learn: Mi perro (my dog), mi gato (my cat).
Pets are part of the family.
Tengo un perro: I have a dog.
check: Tengo un perro means I have a...
Pets can be part of the...
lessons.try: Tell the class about a pet you have or want.

learn: Te quiero means I love you (to family).
Un abrazo is a hug.
Un beso is a kiss.
lessons.try: Make a card that says Te quiero.

learn: Mamá, papá, hermanos.
Abuelos, tíos, primos.
Casa and pets.
lessons.try: Present your family picture in Spanish.

learn: El perro is the dog. El gato is the cat.
El pez is the fish. El pájaro is the bird.
A dog says guau guau in Spanish, not woof woof!
lessons.try: Act like a perro, then a gato, then a pájaro.

learn: La vaca is the cow. El caballo is the horse. El cerdo is the pig.
La gallina is the hen, and she says cocoroco or pío pío for chicks.
Farm animals give us food like milk and eggs.
lessons.try: Sing about farm animals and say each name in Spanish.

learn: El león is the lion. El elefante is the elephant. El mono is the monkey.
La tortuga is the turtle. She is very slow.
Many wild animal words sound a lot like English words.
lessons.try: Pretend to be a león, an elefante and a tortuga.

learn: In Spanish, a dog says guau guau.
A cat says miau.
A rooster says quiquiriquí.
lessons.try: Play an animal sound guessing game.

learn: Pez is fish.
Ballena is whale.
Tortuga is turtle.
lessons.try: Draw an ocean with three sea animals.

learn: Grande means big; pequeño means small.
El elefante es grande.
El ratón es pequeño.
check: Is an elephant grande or pequeño?
lessons.try: Sort animal cards by grande and pequeño.

learn: Salta como un conejo (jump like a rabbit).
Nada como un pez (swim like a fish).
Vuela como un pájaro (fly like a bird).
lessons.try: Play "Simón dice" with animal moves.

learn: El perro es café.
La rana es verde.
El pájaro es azul.
check: La rana es verde means the frog is...
lessons.try: Colour animals and say their colours.

learn: Pets, farm and wild.
Sea animals.
Sounds and moves.
lessons.try: Animal charades in Spanish.

learn: La cabeza is the head. Los ojos are the eyes.
La nariz is the nose. La boca is the mouth. Las orejas are the ears.
Touch each part as you say it.
lessons.try: Touch your cabeza, ojos, nariz and boca as fast as you can.

learn: La mano is the hand. El brazo is the arm.
La pierna is the leg. El pie is the foot.
Mueve means move. Mueve las manos means move your hands.
lessons.try: A grown-up says mueve and a body part. You move it!

learn: Los hombros are the shoulders. Las rodillas are the knees. Los dedos are the fingers or toes.
There is a Spanish song: cabeza, hombros, rodillas y pies.
Y means and.
lessons.try: Sing cabeza, hombros, rodillas y pies and touch each part.

learn: Mano is hand; manos are hands.
Pie is foot; pies are feet.
Dedos are fingers or toes.
lessons.try: Trace your hand and label los dedos.

learn: Tócate la nariz: touch your nose.
Tócate la boca: touch your mouth.
Listen and touch.
check: Tócate la nariz means touch your...
lessons.try: Play "Tócate..." with a partner.

learn: Me lavo las manos: I wash my hands.
Me cepillo los dientes: I brush my teeth.
Healthy habits in Spanish.
check: Me lavo las manos means I wash my...
lessons.try: Act out washing hands and brushing teeth.

learn: Draw a monster with tres ojos (three eyes).
Cuatro brazos (four arms).
Describe it in Spanish.
lessons.try: Draw and describe a silly monster.

learn: Me duele means it hurts.
Me duele la cabeza: my head hurts.
Tell a grown-up if something hurts.
check: Me duele la cabeza means my ___ hurts.
lessons.try: Role-play visiting the nurse.

learn: Cabeza, ojos, nariz, boca.
Brazos, piernas, manos, pies.
Healthy habits.
lessons.try: Sing the body song with actions.

learn: La manzana is the apple. El plátano is the banana. La naranja is the orange.
Las uvas are grapes. Fruit is sweet and good for you.
Me gusta means I like. Me gusta la manzana means I like the apple.
lessons.try: Eat a fruit and say me gusta and its name.

learn: El pan is bread. El queso is cheese. El arroz is rice.
La leche is milk. El agua is water.
Tengo hambre means I am hungry.
lessons.try: At lunch, name three foods on your plate in Spanish.

learn: Sí means yes. No means no in both languages!
No me gusta means I do not like it.
It is fine to say no me gusta politely, and still say gracias.
lessons.try: Ask someone ¿te gusta el queso? They answer sí or no.

learn: Leche is milk.
Pan is bread.
Huevos are eggs.
lessons.try: Draw your breakfast and label it.

learn: Me gusta la manzana: I like the apple.
No me gusta: I don't like.
Share what you like.
check: Me gusta el pan means I like...
lessons.try: Say one food you like and one you don't.

learn: Agua is water.
Jugo is juice.
Quiero agua, por favor: I want water, please.
lessons.try: Ask for a drink politely.

learn: El mercado is the market.
Buy fruit: plátanos, uvas, naranjas.
Count what you buy.
lessons.try: Play market with pretend fruit.

learn: Tengo hambre: I am hungry.
Tengo sed: I am thirsty.
Say it when you need food or water.
check: If you have sed, you need...
lessons.try: Act out hambre and sed.

learn: Fruit and lunch foods.
Me gusta.
Hambre and sed.
lessons.try: Plan a picnic menu in Spanish.

learn: Feliz means happy. Triste means sad.
Estoy feliz means I am happy.
Make a big smile for feliz and a frown for triste.
lessons.try: Make a feliz face and a triste face in a mirror.

learn: To ask how are you, say ¿cómo estás?
You can answer muy bien (very well), bien (fine) or mal (not good).
If a friend says mal, you can ask what is wrong and be kind.
lessons.try: Ask three people ¿cómo estás? today.

learn: Cansado means tired. Enojado means angry. Asustado means scared.
All feelings are okay. We can name them and take a deep breath.
Tengo sueño means I am sleepy.
check: What helps when we feel enojado?
lessons.try: Act out cansado, enojado and asustado. A grown-up guesses which one.

learn: Emocionado or emocionada: excited.
Sorprendido or sorprendida: surprised.
Show the faces.
check: A surprise party makes us feel...
lessons.try: Make excited and surprised faces.

learn: Draw caras (faces) for each feeling.
Name each one.
Feelings change.
lessons.try: Make a feelings wheel.

learn: Respira: breathe.
Cuenta hasta diez: count to ten.
Calma means calm.
check: Cuenta hasta diez means count to...
lessons.try: Practise breathing and counting in Spanish.

learn: ¿Estás bien? Are you okay?
Lo siento: I'm sorry.
Kind words help feelings.
lessons.try: Role-play helping a sad friend.

learn: Sing "Si estás feliz" (If you're happy).
Clap your hands.
Change the feeling each verse.
check: Si estás feliz means If you're...
The song asks us to ___ our hands.
lessons.try: Sing the feelings song with motions.

learn: Feliz, triste, cansado.
¿Cómo estás?
Kind words.
lessons.try: Feelings charades.

learn: Una fiesta is a party. Feliz cumpleaños means happy birthday.
At many birthday parties children break a piñata full of treats.
The piñata is hung up, and children take turns trying to hit it.
lessons.try: Sing feliz cumpleaños to a toy or a friend.

learn: Many children sing counting songs in Spanish, clapping on each number.
Clapping helps you remember words.
Practice uno to diez and back again: diez, nueve, ocho...
check: Counting down from diez, what comes next?
lessons.try: Clap and count to diez, then count back down to uno.

learn: Spanish is spoken by hundreds of millions of people in many countries.
Mexico, Spain, Colombia, Argentina and Puerto Rico are some places where people speak Spanish.
Arizona is next to Mexico, so many neighbors speak Spanish too.
check: Which country next to Arizona speaks Spanish?
Is Spanish spoken in many countries?
lessons.try: Find Mexico on a map or globe with a grown-up.

learn: Día de los Muertos honours family who have died.
Families make altars with photos and marigolds.
Cempasúchil is the marigold flower.
check: Día de los Muertos honours family who have...
lessons.try: Make a paper marigold.

learn: A piñata is a decorated container filled with treats.
Children take turns hitting it.
Sing "Dale, dale, dale".
lessons.try: Make a paper piñata.

learn: A birthday song from Mexico.
Sung in the morning.
Families sing it together.
check: It is often sung in the...
lessons.try: Listen to and hum the birthday song.

learn: Día de Reyes is on January 6.
Children leave shoes for gifts.
Families share rosca de reyes bread.
check: Día de Reyes is on January...
lessons.try: Draw a rosca de reyes.

learn: Spanish is spoken in Mexico, Spain, Argentina and many more.
Over 20 countries speak Spanish.
Find them on a map.
check: Spanish is spoken in about ___ countries.
lessons.try: Colour Spanish-speaking countries on a map.

learn: Fiesta songs.
Holidays.
The Spanish-speaking world.
lessons.try: Hold a class fiesta.
